_about: Decode locks: bills whose decode a person corrected by hand. Read by scripts/decode-locks.mjs; the full rules are in that file's header.
A locked bill is never re-decoded by any pipeline path (nightly new-text re-decode, FORCE_REDECODE_SLUGS, the newsdesk's two re-decode triggers) and never touched by the one-off decode scripts.

Each lock records the text version the correction was checked against (text_version_date, text_version_type, text_version_count, copied from data/bills.json when the lock was made; null means bills.json had no value).

While Congress serves that same version the bill is skipped with one log line. When Congress publishes a NEWER version (later date, different type, a higher count, or a new title) the bill is STILL skipped, and every run that sees it prints '::warning::DECODE LOCK STALE: <slug> ...', which the pipeline-health report raises as the 'decode-lock-stale' alarm.

To act on that alarm, a person re-reads the new text against the corrected decode, then either deletes the lock (the next nightly re-decodes the bill from the new text; add it to FORCE_REDECODE_SLUGS to do it at once) or, if the correction still holds, updates the three version fields to the new version and the locked_on date.

hr-9237-119.reason: Hand-corrected: the new monthly payment (sec. 104) goes to the veteran who gets the aid-and-attendance allowance, not to spouses; combat-disabled retirees under 20 years get combined pay up to a cap (sec. 101), so 'full' was dropped.

hr-2347-119.reason: Hand-corrected: current law (42 U.S.C. 4336a(g)) already sets the one- and two-year review deadlines; the decode now says the bill keeps them and adds the 90- and 120-day deadlines for other agencies' decisions (sec. 1106).

hr-8800-119.reason: Hand-corrected against the Engrossed in House text: the decode now describes Division E (the SAVE America Act, secs. 4801-4803: documentary proof of U.S. citizenship to register, photo ID to vote in federal elections) and names all five divisions (sec. 2); the multiyear contracts list missiles, not artillery shells (secs. 1839, 1840).

hr-6509-119.reason: Hand-corrected against the Introduced in House text: the 20-a-month limit has no per-patient unit (sec. 2(1)); the new definition of "essentially a copy" is described, not called narrower (sec. 2(2)); inspections come before a large outsourcing facility first compounds any drug and at least every two years (sec. 4(a)). Version fields are from the Congress.gov /text record: data/bills.json had none.
